title: Clarify to Amplify: Unleashing Hidden Value in Commercial Real Estate
excerpt: Explore how clarifying your CRE systems can unlock hidden value, drive ROI, and transform your data infrastructure into a strategic asset.
content:
Unlocking Hidden Value in Commercial Real Estate Through Clarification

In the bustling world of commercial real estate, clarity isn't just beneficial; it's essential. As we delve into the Peak Property Performance® podcast, co-hosts Drew Hall and Bill Douglas emphasize the importance of the first step in their PPP 5C™ framework: Clarify. This step is not just about understanding what you own but uncovering the hidden potential within your property's data and systems. By taking a fresh look at your digital infrastructure, you can unlock previously untapped value, save costs, and even open new revenue streams.

The Importance of Knowing What You Own

Imagine stepping into one of your commercial properties and not knowing which systems are operational, which are dormant, and which could be monetizing your data. This lack of clarity can lead to missed opportunities and increased expenses. As Bill highlighted in the podcast, "Who owns and controls your digital infrastructure?" is a crucial question every CRE owner should be asking.

During the episode, Bill and Drew discussed a scenario involving a forgotten lighting control system that, once activated, saved over $56,000 in energy expenses in the first year. This is a prime example of how clarification can lead to significant financial benefits. By simply understanding and documenting what systems are in place, you can make informed decisions about upgrades, maintenance, and utilization, turning potential liabilities into assets.

Clarifying Ownership and Control of Data

In modern commercial real estate, data is a goldmine. However, the true value of this data is only realized when you have control over it. Drew pointed out, "Even if it's analog, it's still generating data." The challenge lies in identifying what data is being generated, where it resides, and how it can be harnessed to improve building operations.

Understanding the interplay of your building's systems and the data they produce is critical. Many CRE owners may not realize how much data their systems are generating and how this data can be leveraged to optimize performance. By clarifying these elements, you can ensure that your infrastructure not only supports your current needs but also lays the groundwork for future growth and innovation.

The Role of Data in Modern CRE Systems

The transition from analog to digital has revolutionized how buildings operate. With modern systems, data has become more modular and granular, providing insights that weren't previously available. Drew emphasized the importance of having a backbone—a robust network that integrates all these data points seamlessly.

"Imagine the decisions that are being made in real time in every system throughout that campus," Drew explained. "Imagine that you have the ability to know why that decision was just made."

This level of insight allows for more informed decision-making, enabling property owners to optimize operations, reduce costs, and enhance tenant experiences. It underscores the need for a comprehensive audit of your data and digital infrastructure, ensuring that you know what you own and how it can serve your business objectives.

Inquisitive Approach to System Optimization

Being inquisitive is not just about asking questions—it's about challenging assumptions and exploring possibilities. Bill recounted a story of a building engineer who discovered an unused system simply by asking, "What is that?" This curiosity led to significant savings and highlighted the importance of an inquisitive mindset.

Such discoveries are not uncommon. Many buildings have systems that are underutilized or completely forgotten. By conducting a thorough review, as OpticWise often does with a Data and Digital Infrastructure (DDI) audit, CRE owners can uncover hidden gems within their properties. These audits don't just save money; they transform how buildings operate, turning overlooked systems into strategic assets.

"They found $56,000 from a review because of one find," Bill noted. "How many times have we gone into buildings and it looks like a rat nest?"

Case Study: Unlocking ROI Through Clarification

One of the most compelling examples from the podcast involved a building where a dormant lighting system was activated, resulting in a rapid ROI. This case study illustrates how clarifying your systems can lead to substantial financial returns.

The building had a lighting control system installed during construction that remained unused for years. Once brought online, it not only improved energy efficiency but also provided valuable data on occupancy and usage patterns. This data enabled further monetization of common areas and improved tenant satisfaction.

This example serves as a powerful reminder that investments in digital infrastructure should be viewed not as expenses but as strategic assets capable of driving significant returns.

Preparing for the Next C: Connect

As we wrap up the discussion on Clarify, it's clear that understanding your systems and data is just the beginning. The next step in the PPP 5C™ framework is Connect, which we'll explore in the upcoming episodes. Connecting your systems and data creates a cohesive network that supports more advanced analytics and automation.

By clarifying your existing infrastructure, you're setting the stage for the next phase of optimization. This preparation ensures that when you move to the Connect stage, your systems are ready to communicate and collaborate effectively, driving even greater value for your property portfolio.

For more insights and strategies, visit the episode page or explore our book for a comprehensive guide to maximizing the potential of your commercial real estate assets.
